subject: Novara demo: inference readiness & SLA criteria
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@novara.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@novara.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Novara demo: inference readiness & SLA criteria

Hi Jake / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great to see the end-to-end flow; appreciate the clarity on the policy routing and the edge-case examples from your SREs. Per our quick wrap-up, I wanted to summarize the performance targets and proposed next steps so we can align on a MAP. Below are the items I captured during the session — please correct anything I missed.

High-level targets (Novara stated):
- 95th pctl latency (user-facing streaming responses): <= 350ms per token for 512-token average responses
- Sustained throughput (text-gen batch steady state): 2,000 tokens/sec across the fleet during peak (US-east)
- Concurrent active users (streaming sessions): 600 concurrent streams with <10ms per-chunk overhead
- Cold-start concurrency tolerance: spike to 1,200 concurrent sessions for up to 3 minutes with graceful shedding/fallbacks

Technical constraints we noted:
- KV cache must persist across short lived container restarts (session affinity preferred)
- Long-tail users send multi-turn streams with unpredictable inter-chunk gaps (requires robust prefix caching)
- Encryption at-rest + customer-managed KMS for audit scope

Proposed immediate MAP items (owner):
1) SLO checklist & measurement plan (Soojin) — attached spreadsheet; please confirm metric names and thresholds.
2) Concurrency/throughput test plan (Rishi) — load profile, synthetic streams, and sample prompt set.
3) Security/compliance checklist (Aditya) — KMS, audit logs, data flow diagram for SOC2 scope.
4) Commercial/PO path (Marissa) — draft MSA/PO and timeline to sign.

Next steps / asks for Novara:
- Can you confirm the 95p/throughput targets above are accurate? (Jake)
- Can SRE provide a short-run production p95 baseline or perf traces from current infra? (sre@novara.ai)

Attachments: redwood-inference-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO names & thresholds), novara-demo-kvlogs-10-22.zip (demo traces)

I’ll circulate a concise MAP doc tomorrow with owners and dates. Goal: schedule a 2-week canary plan and a procurement milestone by 2026-11-05.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@novara.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@novara.ai>, Novara SRE <sre@novara.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T19:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novara demo: inference readiness & SLA criteria

Thanks, Soojin — nice summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 350ms p95 target is what product wants for the in-chat streaming experience. Note that our user prompts average ~420 tokens when you include system messages; the 512 estimate is fine as a ballpark.
- Throughput target: 2,000 tokens/sec is correct for peak, but that needs to include a 20% headroom for model-effects during long-context generations. So if you can show economics for 2.4k tokens/sec that would be ideal.
- Streaming behavior: we need sub-100ms chunking latency end-to-end (chunk production + network) — the 10ms per-chunk overhead target you wrote is just for server-side processing, right? We intend to measure end-to-end RTT.

SRE note (cc): we can send a 24-hour production perf baseline tomorrow. We’ll redact PII and upload traces.

Also tagging procurement lead Elena so she can comment on contract timelines.

—Jake
Jake Porter
Head of Product, Novara AI
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@novara.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@novara.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novara demo: inference readiness & SLA criteria

Appreciate the clarifications, Jake — that helps a lot. Quick responses inline: 

- p95 target: we’ll keep 350ms as the user-facing objective and call out model-induced headroom separately in the MAP. We’ll produce two cost/perf curves: one sized to 2k tokens/sec + 20% headroom (2.4k) and one optimized to bare 2k for comparison.
- Chunking latency: agreed — the 10ms number I had was purely server-side. We'll include network RTT in the end-to-end tests you requested.

I’ve attached an initial MAP (mutual-action-plan-novara.pdf) and the SLO checklist spreadsheet. Key dates proposed:
- 2026-10-27: Redwood provides concurrency & throughput test plan (Rishi)
- 2026-11-02: Novara uploads 24h perf baseline (SRE)
- 2026-11-09: Start 2-week canary in US-east (both teams)
- 2026-11-05: Commercial milestone: PO/committed capacity (target)

Action items (owners):
- Rishi: synthetic streams + prefix cache validation + test harness (deliverable: runbook + results)
- Marissa: finalize commercial terms and draft PO + MSA redline window
- Aditya: provide KMS integration checklist and SOC2 evidence inventory

Can you confirm those dates work for your procurement & SRE? If so I’ll lock the calendar invites.

Thanks — Soo
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Novara demo: inference readiness & SLA criteria

Adding technical detail for the test plan so everyone has visibility. High-level test matrix we plan to run (deliverable: runbook + raw logs attached as zip):

1) Steady-state throughput sweep
- Goal: validate 2k and 2.4k tokens/sec sustained over 10 min windows without backpressure/p95 violations
- Workload: mixed prompt set (50% short, 50% 400-800 token prompts)
- Metrics to capture: server p95, tail latency (99.9), GPU utilization, batch-size distribution, token-per-second observed

2) Concurrency & spike tolerance
- Goal: 600 sustained concurrent streaming sessions; 1,200 spike for up to 3 minutes
- Technique: maintain long-lived SSE/WebSocket streams with randomized inter-chunk gaps to simulate human typing pauses

3) Prefix/KV cache resilience
- Goal: verify prefix cache hit-rate under container churn and across autoscaler events
- Technique: orchestrate short-lived node restarts and validate KV rehydration and latency deltas

4) End-to-end chunk RTT
- Goal: sub-100ms end-to-end chunk latency on average (network + server). We’ll correlate with Novara SRE's trace samples.

Notes & assumptions:
- We’ll need a sample production prompt corpus (Soojin, can Novara share a 10k prompt sample sanitized?).
- Attachment: novara-demo-kvlogs-10-22.zip contains trace snippets we’ll replay for regression tests.

I’ll post the runbook link to the Drive folder and kick off a brief sync next week to align the harness.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Jake / Elena —

Thanks all for the quick responses. From a commercial standpoint we’re aligned to move forward with the MAP timeline Soo proposed. A couple of commercial checkpoints:

1) Decision criteria for Novara to sign PO:
- Canary shows p95 <= 350ms and sustained throughput within 10% of target for 2 of 3 test windows
- Security checklist items confirmed (KMS + audit logs)
- Agreed fallback policy if canary misses targets (auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant + throttling policy)

2) Proposed PO path: I’ll upload the draft PO to DocuSign by EOD today, with a 7-day review window. If procurement needs additional CLINs for reserved capacity we can append.

3) Quick ask: Elena, if Novara can sign off on the target decision criteria above we’ll lock 2026-11-09 as canary start and schedule a mid-canary checkpoint on 2026-11-16 to evaluate rollout.

I’ll attach the commercial term sheet and the MAP PDF.

Thanks — looking forward to the canary.
